_schema.purpose: Audit verdicts for atoms in docs/roadmap/atomic/dag.json. THIS is where a verdict is recorded — never by editing a generated <ID>.md, which the next generator run discards.
_schema.keys: one per atom id; keys beginning with _ are documentation and are ignored

verdict.confirmed: every done_when clause was checked against the code and holds
verdict.partial: some done_when clauses hold and others do not — say which in notes
verdict.contradicted: the status recorded in dag.json disagrees with the code
verdict.unverifiable: cannot be settled in this repo (needs hardware, a paid key, or an owner action)
verdict.unaudited: the default for an atom nobody has checked; normally absent rather than written

fields.evidence: list of concrete artifacts checked — paths, symbols, test names, measured counts
fields.ui_validated: what was DRIVEN in the running product through real user interaction, or absent if nothing was
fields.notes: the reasoning, especially any clause that did NOT hold
fields.follow_ups: list of PRs or issues opened as a result

_schema.rule: A verdict is a claim about evidence, not a vote. `confirmed` requires naming what was checked; an atom whose evidence is only a path that pre-existed the work is `partial` at best — see tools/audit_landed_atoms.py on why path-only evidence scores TRIVIAL.

RUA-4.by: audit cycle 2 (RUA) — observed, against ARCC governance
evidence: cookie attributes observed at dashboard/handlers/auth.py:239-247 — httponly=True, samesite='Lax', path='/', max_age=ttl, secure=secure_cookies(), and NO Domain attribute. That satisfies every clause of ARCC's Secure Cookie Handling guidance (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite Lax/Strict, Path=/, no wildcard Domain, bounded Max-Age)

token_auth.py:669-685 secure_cookies() returns True only for a declared https public URL and fails to False, with the reasoning written out: Secure on plain http makes the cookie undeliverable, which is how essentially every local install runs
the wss CSP clause holds: server.py:1880 emits connect-src with _ws_csp_sources(), documented as returning '' for a normal local install so the policy stays byte-identical there
tests/test_auth_exposure.py passes (part of the 132-passed run)
RUA-4.notes: PARTIAL, and it produced the cycle's one real finding — issue #2735. The dashboard middleware that sets Cache-Control/Pragma/Expires and a detailed CSP sets NO frame-ancestors directive and NO X-Frame-Options anywhere in src/. frame-ancestors does not fall back to default-src, and frame-src is the opposite control, so nothing restricts who may frame the authenticated dashboard — in exactly the public-exposure scenario this atom hardens. The finding is strong because the project already holds the standard elsewhere: artifacts/deploy.py:109 sets frame-ancestors 'self' with a test asserting it at test_artifact_deploy_serve.py:344. Severity is genuinely reduced by SameSite=Lax (a cross-site frame carries no session cookie), and the issue says so rather than overstating; what remains is login-page UI redressing and the deliberate ?token= path, which SameSite does not cover. FILED rather than fixed because the change would break any legitimate cross-origin embedder (Electron shell, preview panes) and that compatibility check is the part that makes it not a ten-minute job. ARCC's Secure HTTP Headers guidance also asks for Referrer-Policy and X-Content-Type-Options on ALL responses; both exist only on specific artifact/file responses here, and #2735 covers promoting them. I did NOT verify the TOTP or enrollment-code clauses — both need a provisioned credential, same blocker as RUA-3.

OU-1.by: ordered audit pass 1 — observed, not read
evidence: src/personalclaw/onboarding.py:53 STEPS = ('name','essentials','first_success','done'); _ESSENTIALS_SCHEMA carries model/search/speech/channel; the merge is partial at both levels (onboarding.py:145-168) and rejects an out-of-domain step with ValueError

OBSERVED ON DISK, not inferred: after driving the wizard in a real browser on a fresh PERSONALCLAW_HOME, .validate-home/entity_settings/onboarding.json held exactly {step:'done', essentials:{model,search,speech,channel}, first_success:{knowledge,trigger,loop}} — the atom's claimed shape, written by the running gateway
the POST write path works end to end: the name typed into step 1 landed in config.json as user_name='Keyur' (config round-trip contract honoured), and the dashboard then greeted 'Good evening, Keyur'
GET /api/onboarding merges live model readiness with the persisted point (handlers_system.py:638-645), which is what the frontend's single on-mount fetch consumes
OU-1.ui_validated: Drove the 5-step wizard in a real browser (playwright-cli, real clicks and typing, no scripted API calls) on TWO fresh homes, ports 10011 and 10012: step gating (Continue disabled until the field has a value), completed steps collapsing into re-editable 'Go back to step N' summaries, a skipped step reading 'Skipped', migration detection finding Claude Code and Codex on this machine with an explicit statement that credentials are excluded, and the skip-to-dashboard escape.
OU-1.notes: Two things I initially read as defects and then disproved by observing the code, recorded so nobody re-chases them. (1) The UI shows 5 steps while STEPS has 4 — DELIBERATE: Onboarding.tsx:146-152 states the import step is intentionally not a stored resume point because item identity is a fingerprint and the importer keeps its own ledger, so a reload there redoes an idempotent step. (2) Typing a name, clicking Continue and reloading LOSES the name (observed: user_name stayed '' and onboarding.json was still absent 12s later, ruling out a debounce; the reload restarted at step 1). Also DELIBERATE: finish() commits identity LAST because user_name IS the `onboarded` route guard (Onboarding.tsx:188-189), so an early write would release the guard mid-flow. The cost is retyping one field and the flow is documented as 'guidance, never a gate'. Neither is an issue; no PR, no issue filed.
